claim: Screen use for ages 2–4 should be limited and should not displace movement, sleep, play, reading or caregiver interaction
design_decision: Default sessions 5–7 minutes; parent cap; no autoplay, streaks or retention loops

claim: High-quality media is more useful when an adult co-views and connects it to real life
design_decision: Co-play prompt and real-world extension for every game

claim: Educational apps should be active, engaged, meaningful and socially interactive around a clear learning goal
evidence_strength: conceptual framework supported by learning science
design_decision: One primary learning goal per game; reject decorative interactions

claim: Executive-function skills develop through interaction and repeated practice
design_decision: Include working memory, inhibition and flexible-rule mechanics across age bands

claim: Working-memory training produces stronger trained/near-task effects than broad far transfer
design_decision: Never claim IQ growth; report only practice on similar tasks

claim: Guided play can support some early math, shape and task-switching outcomes
design_decision: Use child choice plus light adult guidance; avoid drill-only sessions

claim: Developmental milestones orient discussion but do not diagnose or replace screening
design_decision: Age is initial placement only; no developmental diagnosis or age percentile

claim: Child-directed apps should minimize data and gate links or purchases
design_decision: Offline-only v1; no ads, analytics, identifiers, permissions or child-mode links

claim: Children receive additional safeguards under EU data-protection law
evidence_strength: high for legal principle; implementation requires jurisdiction review
design_decision: No online personal data; clear parent disclosure; local export and deletion
